content: Actinic conjunctivitis, also known by terms such as Klieg conjunctivitis, eye burn, arc-flash, welder's conjunctivitis, flash keratoconjunctivitis, actinic ray ophthalmia, or ultraviolet ray ophthalmia, is an ocular condition caused by prolonged exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation. The condition is characterized by symptoms including redness and swelling of the eyes. It is most commonly associated with extended exposure to intense light sources such as Klieg lights, therapeutic lamps, and acetylene torches. Historically, actinic conjunctivitis has been reported in unusual contexts, including by individuals claiming to have witnessed unidentified flying objects (UFOs). Specifically, the condition is referenced under the term Klieg conjunctivitis in relation to the Mothman case in Point Pleasant, West Virginia. This association is documented in John A. Keel's book, The Mothman Prophecies.
